summary: Monika Nowakowska works in Indology and philosophy. She was attested as holding a post at the University of Warsaw in 2010 and 2026.

Monika Zin specializes in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich, she held professorships at Munich (~2001–2015) and FU Berlin (~2014–2016), later working at Leipzig.
Moodeen Sheriff was active in medicine and Indology. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman, he held posts at Sendai National College of Technology and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist. After studying at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, he served at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884, succeeding Gauss in 1858.

Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has held posts at Musashino University and served as director of the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies (attested 2002).

Moriz Haupt was a Germanist and classicist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Leipzig (1841–1851) and Berlin (from 1853), and served as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1861–1874).

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Georg Bühler at Vienna and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at Oxford, the German University in Prague (~1902–1934), and Visva-Bharati University (1922–1924).

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He has taught at Yale, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London. He directed the National Museum of Wales, the London Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948), and founded the UCL Institute of Archaeology.

Morton Klass worked in anthropology and religious studies. Educated at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, where he studied under Conrad M. Arensberg, he held posts at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin as his disciple and later succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama, and spent much of his career at Shuchiin University as a lecturer and professor from 1973.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Yasunori Ejima and at the University of Vienna, later serving as an associate professor at Tsukuba (~1996–2023).

Mou Zongsan was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and under Shili Xiong. He taught at several institutions, including National Taiwan University, Tunghai University, the University of Hong Kong, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.
Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and has been a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1990) and as a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982–1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and has held posts at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum and held directorships at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and Quaid-i-Azam University.
